question:
A mobile manufacturing company produces three types of smartphones: Alpha, Beta, and Gamma. The sales data for two consecutive years in two regions (Region X and Region Y) is represented by matrices A and B respectively as follows:

$A = \begin{bmatrix}200 & 180 & 120 \\ 150 & 210 & 160\end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix}220 & 170 & 135 \\ 160 & 200 & 175\end{bmatrix}$

(Row 1 corresponds to Region X, Row 2 to Region Y; Columns correspond to Alpha, Beta, Gamma.)

(i) Calculate the total increase in sales for each smartphone in each region over the two years.

(ii) Find the average sales for each model in each region across the two years.

(iii) Verify if the matrix representing the increase in sales between the years is a zero matrix.

(iv) If the price of each phone is given by the column vector $P = \begin{bmatrix}20,000 \\ 25,000 \\ 30,000\end{bmatrix}$, compute the total revenue generated in each region for each year.

(v) Compare the revenue matrices and comment on which region and year were most profitable.
explanation:
(i) The increase in sales matrix = B - A:

$B - A = \begin{bmatrix}220-200 & 170-180 & 135-120 \\ 160-150 & 200-210 & 175-160\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}20 & -10 & 15 \\ 10 & -10 & 15\end{bmatrix}$

(ii) Average sales matrix for two years:

$\frac{A+B}{2} = \begin{bmatrix}\frac{200+220}{2} & \frac{180+170}{2} & \frac{120+135}{2} \\ \frac{150+160}{2} & \frac{210+200}{2} & \frac{160+175}{2}\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}210 & 175 & 127.5 \\ 155 & 205 & 167.5\end{bmatrix}$

(iii) The increase in sales matrix is $\begin{bmatrix}20 & -10 & 15 \\ 10 & -10 & 15\end{bmatrix}$, which is not a zero matrix as not all elements are zero.

(iv) Total revenue for each region each year (using matrix multiplication):

For A (Year 1): $A \times P$

$\begin{bmatrix}200 & 180 & 120 \\ 150 & 210 & 160\end{bmatrix} \times \begin{bmatrix}20,000 \\ 25,000 \\ 30,000\end{bmatrix}$

First row: $(200 \times 20,000) + (180 \times 25,000) + (120 \times 30,000) = 4,000,000 + 4,500,000 + 3,600,000 = 12,100,000$

Second row: $(150 \times 20,000) + (210 \times 25,000) + (160 \times 30,000) = 3,000,000 + 5,250,000 + 4,800,000 = 13,050,000$

So for Year 1: $\begin{bmatrix}12,100,000 \\ 13,050,000\end{bmatrix}$

For B (Year 2): $B \times P$

First row: $(220 \times 20,000) + (170 \times 25,000) + (135 \times 30,000) = 4,400,000 + 4,250,000 + 4,050,000 = 12,700,000$

Second row: $(160 \times 20,000) + (200 \times 25,000) + (175 \times 30,000) = 3,200,000 + 5,000,000 + 5,250,000 = 13,450,000$

So for Year 2: $\begin{bmatrix}12,700,000 \\ 13,450,000\end{bmatrix}$

(v) Comparing revenue:

For Year 1, Region Y had the highest revenue ($13,050,000$). For Year 2, Region Y also had the highest ($13,450,000$). The most profitable was Region Y in Year 2.

options.A:
(i) Increase matrix $=\begin{bmatrix}210&175&127.5\\155&205&167.5\end{bmatrix}$.
(ii) Average matrix $=\begin{bmatrix}20&-10&15\\10&-10&15\end{bmatrix}$.
(iii) Increase matrix is zero.
(iv) Year 1 revenue $=\begin{bmatrix}12700000\\13450000\end{bmatrix}$, Year 2 revenue $=\begin{bmatrix}12100000\\13050000\end{bmatrix}$.
(v) Region X in Year 1 was most profitable.
options.B:
(i) Increase matrix $B-A=\begin{bmatrix}20&-10&15\\10&-10&15\end{bmatrix}$.
(ii) Average sales matrix $=\begin{bmatrix}210&175&127.5\\155&205&167.5\end{bmatrix}$.
(iii) The increase matrix is not a zero matrix.
(iv) Year 1 revenue $=\begin{bmatrix}12100000\\13050000\end{bmatrix}$ and Year 2 revenue $=\begin{bmatrix}12700000\\13450000\end{bmatrix}$.
(v) Region Y in Year 2 was most profitable.
options.C:
(i) Increase matrix $A-B=\begin{bmatrix}20&-10&15\\10&-10&15\end{bmatrix}$.
(ii) Average sales matrix is zero.
(iii) Increase matrix is zero.
(iv) Revenue cannot be computed because multiplication is not defined.
(v) No region is profitable.
options.D:
(i) Increase matrix $=A+B$.
(ii) Average matrix $=B-A$.
(iii) Increase matrix is identity.
(iv) Revenue is the same in both years.
(v) Region X in Year 2 was most profitable.
